title: Pan-genomics Analysis Using R and Micropan
author: Frank O Aylward
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.zekf3cw

steps.title: Download Tutorial Data
steps.instruction: Clone the tutorial repository from GitHub to obtain the necessary source code and protein files.

substeps.instruction: Run: git clone https://github.com/faylward/pangenomics_tutorial
Navigate to the directory: cd pangenomics_tutorial
Verify files (micropan-source.R and 4 gzipped .faa files) using: ls -la

steps.title: Decompress Protein Files
steps.instruction: Unzip the .faa files located in the fasta/ folder.

substeps.instruction: Run: gunzip fasta/*.faa.gz
Verify decompression with: ls -la fasta

steps.title: Run Proteinortho Analysis
steps.instruction: Calculate orthologous groups for the protein files using proteinortho5.

substeps.instruction: Run: proteinortho5 -project=cp_pangenome -cpus=2 -singles fasta/*.faa
Verify output file creation with: ls -la

steps.title: Inspect Proteinortho Output
steps.instruction: Analyze the resulting .proteinortho file to determine the number of protein clusters.

substeps.instruction: Use 'head' and 'tail' to inspect the tab-delimited format.
Count total protein clusters by running: wc -l cp_pangenome.proteinortho and subtracting one for the header.

steps.title: Initialize R Session and Load Micropan
steps.instruction: Start an R environment and load the micropan source code.

substeps.instruction: Start R by typing: R
Load the source code using the source() function, specifying the correct path to micropan-source.R (e.g., source("week7/pangenomics_tutorial/micropan-source.R")).

steps.title: Import Data into R
steps.instruction: Load the Proteinortho results into R and convert them into a pangenome matrix object.

substeps.instruction: Create a DataFrame 'x' by running: x <- read.table("week7/pangenomics_tutorial/cp_pangenome.proteinortho", header=T, sep="\t")
Transform the data into a pangenome matrix: panmat <- as.panmat(x)

steps.title: Generate Pan-genome Summary
steps.instruction: Use the micropan summary function to verify the statistics of the pangenome matrix.

substeps.instruction: Run: summary(panmat)

steps.title: Calculate Rarefaction Curve
steps.instruction: Determine the rate of new protein identification as more genomes are added.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the curve with 100 permutations: rarefy <- rarefaction(panmat, n.perm=100)
View results: summary(rarefy)

steps.title: Plot Rarefaction Curve
steps.instruction: Visualize the rarefaction results and save the output as a JPEG image.

substeps.instruction: Initialize JPEG file: jpeg("rarefaction.jpg")
Plot the graph with y-axis limits from 0 to the max rarefaction value: plot(rarefy, ylim=c(0, max(rarefy)))
Close the graphical device: dev.off()

steps.title: Analyze Protein Cluster Distribution
steps.instruction: Use Unix commands to identify shared and unique protein clusters from the .proteinortho file.

substeps.instruction: Find proteins shared by all 5 genomes (exactly one time): cut -f 1-2 cp_pangenome.proteinortho | grep -P "5\t5" | wc | wc -l
Find singleton clusters (present once in one genome): cut -f 1-2 cp_pangenome.proteinortho | grep -P "1\t1" | wc | wc -l

steps.title: Calculate Chao Statistic
steps.instruction: Estimate the total number of genes expected if infinitely many genomes were sequenced.

substeps.instruction: Run in R: chao(panmat)

steps.title: Estimate Pan-genome Diversity via Heaps Law
steps.instruction: Calculate the alpha parameter to determine if the pan-genome is 'open' (alpha < 1) or 'closed' (alpha > 1).

substeps.instruction: Run in R with 1000 permutations: heap <- heaps(panmat, 1000)
